steps.what: Weigh letters and parcels and note the weight
Compute mailing costs based on the destination
Review the correct postage against the item
Affix the correct postage to the item

tasks.design: The clerk weighs letters and parcels on the counter scale. {OPS_SYSTEM} computes the mailing cost from the stored rate for that class, weight, and destination. A destination that is not on the card stays blank. The clerk reviews the amount and affixes the postage.
tasks.previous_blocker: The rate lived on a paper chart, and the clerk re-read it for every item.
tasks.enabler_now: The rate card is in the counter system, so a known lane prices itself.
tasks.still_hard: Weighing the item and affixing the postage stay at the counter.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk judges an item the card does not price, and puts the postage on.

ambition.what: An ordinary item is priced while the customer waits, and the clerk still affixes the postage.

tasks.altitude: The clerk sees the amount before the postage goes on.

reach.learn: Which class and destination were priced.

evidence.claim: A rate card returns postage from stored weight, class, and destination. A stored rate or form can be filled when weight, destination, service, and amount are already fields. The clerk still handles the item, the cash, and the signature. A payout or a filing stops when a stored id does not match.

The source pack says tools that log who did what, and schedules based on behaviour, need consent where a works council has that right. This work does not score clerks. Paying out, filing a theft report, or sending a referral is signed by the clerk. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when an item is at the counter and ends when the postage is affixed or the clerk has refused the price.
A rate row has class, weight band, destination, and amount, maintained by the pricing owner. A missing row is left blank.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the clerk's effort.
A missing weight, amount, or form field is not invented. The clerk does that part.
The incremental hour updates the opened record when its source row changes.
unknowns: How often a destination is missing from the card.
research_questions: Which items were priced from the card, and which the clerk priced by hand?

already_counted.description: The counter or review time is already in the clerk's step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

approvals.approved_version: The postage amount for this weight, class, and destination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most destinations are off the card, so the clerk prices them. High: weight, class, and destination are on the card, and only weighing, checking, and affixing remain. The range stays under the net.

steps.what: Open the postage rule for this class
Check packages and letters for correct postage

tasks.design: The postage rule for the class is opened from {OPS_SYSTEM}. The clerk checks packages and letters against it and ensures the item is in proper condition for mailing. The screen does not accept or reject the item.
tasks.previous_blocker: The condition rules were a poster, and the clerk remembered the exceptions.
tasks.enabler_now: The class rule is on the item screen, so the check starts from the written rule.
tasks.still_hard: Looking at the item, and refusing one that is damaged or short-paid, stays with the clerk.
tasks.altitude: The clerk still inspects every item. The rule is only the reference.

evidence.claim: A stored class rule can be opened beside the item. The acceptance decision stays with the person who sees the item. A stored rate or form can be filled when weight, destination, service, and amount are already fields. The clerk still handles the item, the cash, and the signature. A payout or a filing stops when a stored id does not match.

steps.what: Open the plan for incoming and outgoing mail
Sort according to type and destination
Continue operating electronic sorting and scanning devices

tasks.design: The sort plan for incoming and outgoing mail is opened from {OPS_SYSTEM}. The clerk sorts by hand according to type and destination, and keeps operating the electronic sorting and scanning devices. The plan does not move the mail.
tasks.previous_blocker: The destination breaks were a wall chart the clerk re-read.
tasks.enabler_now: The plan is on the run, so the breaks are named before the sort starts.
tasks.still_hard: Handling the pieces and operating the device stay with the clerk.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk sees a piece the plan does not name.
tasks.altitude: The clerk still sorts and operates the device. The plan only names the breaks.

reach.learn: Which destination the bundle was for.

evidence.claim: A stored sort plan can name the destination breaks. Moving and scanning the mail stays with the person at the device. A stored rate or form can be filled when weight, destination, service, and amount are already fields. The clerk still handles the item, the cash, and the signature. A payout or a filing stops when a stored id does not match.

steps.what: Open the registered or special delivery item
Obtain signatures from recipients of special delivery

tasks.design: The registered or special delivery record is opened from {OPS_SYSTEM}. The clerk obtains the signature from the recipient in person. {DOCS} files the signature against that item id. A missing item id is not given a signature.
tasks.previous_blocker: The signature book was separate from the item list, and the clerk copied the item id.
tasks.enabler_now: The item id is already on the delivery record, so the signature is filed against it.
tasks.still_hard: Witnessing the recipient, and refusing a signature that is not theirs, stays with the clerk.
tasks.altitude: The clerk still meets the recipient. Only the copy of the item id is removed.

reach.learn: Which item id was signed for.

evidence.claim: A signature image can be stored against an item id the clerk already opened. The act of obtaining the signature stays in person. A stored rate or form can be filled when weight, destination, service, and amount are already fields. The clerk still handles the item, the cash, and the signature. A payout or a filing stops when a stored id does not match.

The source pack says tools that log who did what, and schedules based on behaviour, need consent where a works council has that right. This work does not score clerks. Paying out, filing a theft report, or sending a referral is signed by the clerk. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a registered or special item is at the counter or the door and ends when the recipient has signed or refused.
A delivery row has item id and service, created when the item was accepted. The signature is an image the clerk captured, not a generated mark.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the clerk's effort.
A missing weight, amount, or form field is not invented. The clerk does that part.
The incremental hour updates the opened record when its source row changes.
unknowns: How often the recipient is not the person named on the item.
research_questions: Which items have a signature filed, and which were refused?
